expl: Nallamalai Hills are situated between the Krishna River and Pennar River, stretched from north to south, parallel to the Coromandel Coast on the Bay of Bengal. Javadi Hills are located on the Eastern Ghats in the Vellore and Tiruvannamalai districts of Tamil Nadu State. Renowned as the ‘Blue Mountains’, Nilgiri Hills are located at the junction of Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats. Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills at 2,637 metres. The Anaimalai or Anamalai Hills form the southern portion of the Western Ghats and span up to the border of Kerala and Tamil Nadu in southern India. Anaimudi is the highest peak in the Anaimalai Hills at 2695 metres. These four hills are located in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Kerala states in India from north to south. Hence, the correct option is (c).

stem: Which one of the following statements is not correct?

options.label: a
options.text: The Western Ghats are relatively high in their Northern region.

options.label: b
options.text: The Anaimudi is the highest peak in the Western Ghats.

options.label: c
options.text: Tapti river lies to the south of Satpura.

options.label: d
options.text: The Narmada and the Tapti river valleys are said to be old rift valleys.

expl: Anaimudi (2695 meters) is the highest peak of southern India as well as in the Western Ghats in India, located in southern region. Hence, statement (b) is correct. Tapti river lies to the south of Satpura. Hence, statement (c) is correct. The rift valley is a linear-shaped lowland between several highlands or mountain ranges created by the action of a geologic rift or fault. Hence Narmada, Damodar & Tapti rivers are examples of Indian rift valleys. Hence, statement (d) is also correct. Statement (a) is wrong because southern part of Western Ghats is relatively high.

stem: Which one of the following mountain ranges is spread over only one state in India?
expl: Ajanta Range : The Ajanta Range is located in Maharashtra. It is a mountain range that is spread over only one state. The others are expanded to more than one state. Satpura Range : The Satpura Range is a range of hills in Central India. The range rises in eastern Gujarat, running east through the border of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh to the east of Chhattisgarh. Aravalli Range: The Aravalli Range is a range of mountains in western India running approximately 800 km in northeast to southwest direction across the states of Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Haryana ending in Delhi. Sahyadri Range: The Sahyadri Mountain Range or the Western Ghats originates in Gujarat, runs parallel to the Western coast and merges with the Nilgiri hills in the south. These hills cover 1500 km and form the catchment area for complex river drainage systems.
